correctness.rationale: With m=4k and alpha=m-2, beta-moment monomial norms give K=H_{m,beta}(s)/(1-s)^m, and odd numerator F=(1+s)^m H(s)-(1-s)^m H(-s). At beta=0, finite simple roots are s=i tan(pi j/m), with exactly 2k-1 strictly interior and the two critical ±i on |s|=1. Differentiation of the numerator at (0,i) gives s_+'(0)=2i S_{4k}/m, where S_{4k}=sum_{j<k}(-4)^j[1/(4j+1)+2/(4j+2)+2/(4j+3)]. Positive block magnitudes 4^j A_j strictly increase, including j=0→1, so the alternating sum has sign (-1)^(k-1) for all k; root continuity proves inward/outward crossing and exact disk count 2k+(-1)^(k-1) for sufficiently small beta<0. Independently recomputed S_{4k} with Fraction arithmetic for k=1..8, including slope -16/105 for k=2. The origin is a numerator zero, not an attainable nonzero scalar for two punctured-disk points; count of fibers is one less. Finite checks do not prove the infinite sign law.
